question: Among these, which state experienced a population of over 100 million as per 2011 Census?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Bihar** had a population of approximately **104.1 million** as per the **2011 Census**, making it the **third most populous state** in India after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra. 
• The **2011 Census of India** is conducted every 10 years by the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India**, providing detailed demographic statistics. 
• Bihar has a relatively **small geographical area of 94,163 square kilometers** but a very **high population density**. In 2011, the population density was recorded at **1,106 persons per square kilometer**. 
• Bihar’s population growth is driven by factors such as **high birth rates**, a **young population**, and **rural migration patterns**. 
• Other populous states such as **West Bengal** (91.3 million), **Madhya Pradesh** (72.6 million), and **Rajasthan** (68.5 million) had populations below **100 million** as per the **2011 Census**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Population of India:** 
• The **total population** of India as per the **2011 Census** was approximately **1.21 billion**, making India the **second most populous country** in the world after China. 
• India’s population is distributed across **28 states** and **8 Union territories**. 
• **Uttar Pradesh** is the most populous state, followed by **Maharashtra** and **Bihar**. 
• **Population Density:** 
• **Bihar** has one of the **highest population densities** in India, reflecting a high concentration of people within a limited geographical area. 
• The population density of Bihar was recorded at **1,106 persons per square kilometer** in **2011**. 
• **Demographic Challenges in Bihar:** 
• Bihar faces challenges due to its **high population growth rate**, which puts immense pressure on resources and infrastructure. 
• The state has a **low literacy rate** and challenges in healthcare, making population management a critical issue. 
• Bihar has a significant proportion of its population living in **rural areas**, emphasizing the need for rural development initiatives. 
• **Significance of Census Data:** 
• The **Census** provides crucial data for planning and implementing government policies such as **resource allocation**, **infrastructure development**, and **socio-economic programs**. 
• The **2011 Census** was the **15th National Census of India**, offering valuable insights into demographics, literacy, employment, housing, and migration patterns. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Rural and Urban Divide:** 
• A large proportion of Bihar’s population resides in **rural areas**, which necessitates focused development in sectors like **agriculture**, **education**, and **healthcare**. 
• **Decadal Growth Rate:** 
• Bihar’s population growth rate between **2001** and **2011** was approximately **25.42%**, one of the **highest** among Indian states. 
• **Migration Patterns:** 
• Bihar has a significant number of migrants moving to other states for **employment opportunities**, influencing socio-economic dynamics across India. 
• **Government Initiatives:** 
• The government has introduced several schemes to address challenges related to **population growth**, **healthcare**, and **education** in Bihar. 
c0:T23
